subtitle: How a vassal’s son carved sovereignty in Telugu stone

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of a lone king before a great stone slab in Hanamakonda fort
panels.action: Rudradeva of Anumakonda stands in armour and simple royal cloth, hand resting on an unfinished inscription-stone amid half-built fort walls and watching nobles, the Deccan sky burning orange over Warangal’s emerging bastions.

dialogue.text: In 1163, Rudradeva of Anumakonda did something no overlord had asked of him: he carved his power in Telugu stone, and a vassal house began to speak as a kingdom.

i18n.hi: ११६३ में अनुमकोंडा के रुद्रदेव ने अनोखा काम किया — तेलुगू पत्थर पर अपना अधिकार उकेरा, और एक सामंती घराने की आवाज़ राज जैसी हो गई।

panels.shot: sweeping bird’s-eye over the Deccan plateau
panels.action: A vast Deccan landscape stretches with dry plains, rocky outcrops and scattered villages, distant fortified towns marking Rashtrakuta and Chalukya domains under a hazy monsoon sky.

dialogue.text: For two centuries before Rudradeva, the Deccan was a chessboard of power. Rashtrakutas, then Chalukyas, moved pieces. The Kakatiya chiefs were only small carved pawns on this board.

i18n.hi: रुद्रदेव से दो सौ साल पहले, दक्कन सत्ता की शतरंज थी। पहले राष्ट्रकूट, फिर चालुक्य, मोहरे चलते रहे। काकतीय सरदार बस छोटे तराशे हुए प्यादे थे।

panels.shot: close-up on ancient copper plates laid out on a scholar’s desk
panels.action: An aged hand gently spreads open the Mangallu copper-plate grant, its engraved Sanskrit letters glinting under lamplight, with other early plates stacked nearby.

dialogue.text: Our trail begins not in legend but on copper. The Mangallu plates of 956 name early ancestors, linked to Rashtrakuta service, described plainly as Shudras, village men who served rather than ruled.

i18n.hi: हमारी कहानी दंतकथा से नहीं, ताम्रपत्र से शुरू होती है। ९५६ के मंगल्लु पट्टों में आरंभिक पुरखे दर्ज हैं, राष्ट्रकूट सेवा से जुड़े, सीधे-सीधे शूद्र कहे गए, गाँव के लोग जो राज नहीं, सेवा करते थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of a rustic tank in the countryside at sunrise
panels.action: A broad irrigation tank gleams in morning light, bunds lined with stones, farmers walking along the edge, a weathered inscribed slab standing silently by the water.

dialogue.text: At Bayyaram a tank and a stone remember them again. These chiefs managed water, fields, and small strongholds under greater lords. Their world was duty, not destiny.

i18n.hi: बय्यारम में एक तालाब और पत्थर उन्हें फिर याद करते हैं। ये सरदार पानी, खेत और छोटे दुर्ग संभालते थे, बड़े मालिकों के अधीन। उनका संसार कर्तव्य का था, नियति का नहीं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on the Sanigaram inscription set into a temple wall
panels.action: A temple wall of creamy stone holds the Sanigaram inscription; faint letters run across its face as pilgrims pass by, barely glancing at the record carved centuries ago.

dialogue.text: By 1149, the Sanigaram inscription shows Prola II still a vassal, his loyalty tied to the Chalukya house. A capable commander, but speaking always in another king’s name.

i18n.hi: ११४९ तक, सानिगारं शिलालेख में प्रोल-२ अब भी सामंत है, निष्ठा चालुक्य घराने से बंधी। हुनरमंद सेनानायक, पर बात हमेशा किसी और राजा की।

panels.shot: sweeping wide of a battlefield camp under stormy skies
panels.action: A Deccan war camp sprawls near rocky hills: banner poles, tethered horses, ranks of spearmen, with a distant central pavilion bearing the crest of Western Chalukyas.

dialogue.text: Around these stones raged a larger struggle. Western Chalukyas fought for the Deccan. Feudatories watched the sky like soldiers at sea, waiting to see which banner would survive the storm.

i18n.hi: इन पत्थरों के चारों ओर बड़ी जंग चल रही थी। पश्चिमी चालुक्य दक्कन के लिए लड़ते रहे। सामंत आसमान को टकटकी लगाए नाविक सैनिकों जैसे देखते, कि तूफ़ान के बाद कौन सा ध्वज बचता है।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a dim royal tent, torchlit
panels.action: Young Rudradeva stands beside an older noble in a Chalukya war tent, map spread on a low table, torchlight throwing sharp shadows across his focused face and simple warrior’s dress.

dialogue.text: Into this world Rudradeva was born, heir to Prola II’s responsibilities and his limits. A vassal’s son, raised among maps and musters, knowing his house was strong yet second.

i18n.hi: इसी दुनिया में रुद्रदेव जन्मा, प्रोल-२ की जिम्मेदारियों और सीमाओं का वारिस। सामंत का बेटा, नक्शों और फौजी जमाव के बीच बड़ा हुआ, जानता था उसका घर मजबूत है, पर दूसरा दर्जा।

panels.shot: low-angle wide shot of Anumakonda fortifying works
panels.action: Rudradeva oversees stone masons and labourers strengthening Anumakonda’s walls, standing on a rampart with a measuring staff, eyes scanning the horizon where fields meet scrub forest.

dialogue.text: At Anumakonda he hardened walls and hearts. Forts, tanks, and village ties became his field of rule. Power did not start with crowns, but with stone set well and people bound close.

i18n.hi: अनुमकोंडा में उसने दीवारें भी सख्त कीं, दिल भी। किले, तालाब और गाँव की डोर ही उसका राजक्षेत्र बने। ताकत ताज से नहीं, टिके पत्थर और जुड़े लोगों से शुरू हुई।

panels.shot: intimate close-up on Rudradeva’s face at dusk on the ramparts
panels.action: On the fort wall at dusk, Rudradeva gazes toward distant lands, jaw set, a faint glint of ambition in his thoughtful eyes as village fires kindle below.

dialogue.text: If the Chalukya tree withers, must we fall with its shade?

i18n.hi: अगर चालुक्य वृक्ष सूख जाए, तो क्या हमें भी उसकी छाया के साथ गिरना है?

panels.shot: dynamic montage split-screen of crumbling overlord banners and rising local standards
panels.action: One side shows a torn Chalukya banner drooping over a neglected fort; the other shows a fresh local standard being raised before Anumakonda’s stronger walls as villagers watch.

dialogue.text: By mid-twelfth century, the old trunks cracked. Chalukya authority frayed; feudatories pushed roots deeper. In this loosened soil, a family once called Shudra began thinking like rulers.

i18n.hi: बारहवीं सदी के बीच तक पुराने तने चटकने लगे। चालुक्य सत्ता झुलसी; सामंतों ने अपनी जड़ें गहरी धकेलीं। इस ढीली मिट्टी में, एक घराना जो कभी शूद्र कहलाया था, शासक सा सोचने लगा।

panels.shot: medium shot in a temple courtyard with advisers around Rudradeva
panels.action: Rudradeva sits on a simple throne in a temple courtyard, priests and scribes around him, palm-leaf manuscripts and stone drafts on the ground, everyone engaged in serious discussion.

dialogue.text: With overlords distant, a question sharpened in Anumakonda: if you command forts, protect villages, and dispense justice, who are you? Merely a servant, or something more?

i18n.hi: जब मालिक दूर हों, अनुमकोंडा में सवाल और तीखा हुआ: अगर तुम किले संभालो, गाँव बचाओ, न्याय दो — तो तुम कौन हो? सिर्फ नौकर, या कुछ ज्यादा?

panels.shot: tight close-up of a chisel poised above stone, Rudradeva’s hand guiding
panels.action: Rudradeva’s hand rests firm on a stone slab as a sculptor holds a chisel ready; drafts with Telugu script lie nearby, the first letters roughly sketched on the rock.

dialogue.text: Tradition might claim solar kings and ancient heroes, but the record tells a different story. No divine arrow brought the Kakatiyas here; careful hands on stone did.

i18n.hi: परंपरा चाहे सूर्यवंशी राजे और प्राचीन नायक गढ़े, पर लेखी सबूत कुछ और कहते हैं। काकतीयों को यहाँ कोई दिव्य बाण नहीं लाया; उन्हें गढ़ा है पत्थर पर चली सावधान हथेलियों ने।

panels.shot: slow push-in on the Anumakonda inscription being carved
panels.action: Artisans carve neat lines of Telugu script into the Anumakonda inscription slab while Rudradeva watches, armored yet bareheaded, the unfinished fort of Hanamakonda behind him.

dialogue.text: On 19 January 1163, at Anumakonda, a new choice was made. An inscription was ordered in Telugu, declaring Rudradeva’s authority. The language of fields became the tongue of rule.

i18n.hi: १९ जनवरी ११६३ को, अनुमकोंडा में एक नया फैसला हुआ। तेलुगू में शिलालेख गढ़वाया गया, जो रुद्रदेव की सत्ता घोषित करता था। खेतों की भाषा अब राज की बोली बनी।

panels.shot: low-angle side view of Rudradeva as the sculptor looks up for approval
panels.action: The sculptor pauses, looks up from the carved Telugu lines to Rudradeva, who nods with calm resolve, hand resting on his sword hilt, the air thick with dust and anticipation.

dialogue.speaker: rudradeva_of_anumakonda
dialogue.text: Let this stone speak as we do. Let it name no overlord above me.

i18n.hi: ये पत्थर हमारी ज़बान में बोले। ये मेरे ऊपर किसी मालिक का नाम न लिखे।

panels.shot: medium shot of villagers and minor chiefs gathered around the finished slab
panels.action: Villagers, petty chiefs, and temple servants stand around the newly erected inscription stone, tracing the Telugu letters with their eyes as Rudradeva observes from a step above them.

dialogue.text: Those words did more than record gifts. They named Rudradeva as a sovereign, in a tongue his people knew. A vassal family stepped from service into statehood, line by carved line.

i18n.hi: इन शब्दों ने सिर्फ दान नहीं दर्ज किए। इन्होंने रुद्रदेव को स्वामी कहा, उसी ज़बान में जो उसके लोग जानते थे। एक सामंती वंश सेवा से निकलकर राज में कदम रख गया, रेखा-दर-रेखा।

panels.shot: wide shot of Hanamakonda and Warangal region with temples and forts emerging
panels.action: Across the rolling plains, new fort walls rise, shrines dot the landscape, village clusters thicken; the twin centres of Hanamakonda and Warangal begin to take shape under a clear sky.

dialogue.text: From this moment, the Kakatiya story turns. Under Rudradeva, Anumakonda and Hanamakonda become true centres, drawing warriors, merchants, and cultivators into a growing Telugu realm.

i18n.hi: यहीं से काकतीय कथा मोड़ लेती है। रुद्रदेव के नीचे अनुमकोंडा और हनमकोंडा सच्चे केंद्र बनते हैं, जहाँ योद्धा, व्यापारी और किसान जुटकर बढ़ता हुआ तेलुगू राज्य रचते हैं।

panels.shot: conceptual montage of later inscriptions and temples layered over the landscape
panels.action: Layers of later stone inscriptions and temple towers fade over the Deccan hills, Telugu script repeating in different hands, suggesting centuries of continued record-making and rule.

dialogue.text: Later poets would call them Kshatriyas of sun and legend. Yet it was these earlier records, plain and local, that built something lasting: a Telugu political identity shared in stone.

i18n.hi: बाद के कवि उन्हें सूर्यवंशी क्षत्रिय और गाथाओं के वीर कहेंगे। पर असल टिकाऊ धरोहर इन्हीं पुराने, साधे लेखों ने बनाई — पत्थर पर गढ़ी साझा तेलुगू राजनीतिक पहचान।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on the Telugu letters of Rudradeva’s name with his shadow falling over them
panels.action: The carved Telugu letters of Rudradeva’s name fill the frame, crisp and deep, as his shadow stretches across the stone, hinting at a figure just out of view.

dialogue.text: Rudradeva did not change his birth; he changed his record. By choosing Telugu stone and a sovereign voice, he began a future in which the people’s language could carry the weight of a crown.

i18n.hi: रुद्रदेव ने अपना जन्म नहीं बदला, अपनी दास्तान बदली। तेलुगू पत्थर और स्वाधीन आवाज़ चुनकर उसने वह भविष्य शुरू किया, जिसमें लोगों की भाषा भी ताज का भार उठा सके।

title_i18n.en: The Vassals Who Chose Telugu Stone
title_i18n.hi: वे सामंत जिन्होंने चुना तेलुगू पत्थर

subtitle_i18n.en: How a vassal’s son carved sovereignty in Telugu stone
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक सामंत के बेटे ने तेलुगू पत्थर पर अपना राज गढ़ा
